exposure: One-on-one continuous professional support during labor (midwife, doula)
outcome: Flow state levels (measure of childbirth experience)
cohort: The study included 788 women with previous childbirth experience who were recruited via social media.
finding: One-on-one continuous professional support provided by midwives or doulas was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of physiological birth and lower medical interventions, as well as heightened flow state levels during childbirth.
mod_finding: One-on-one professional support was significantly associated with natural childbirth (a mode of birth) and lower medical interventions compared to conventional assistance.
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively after childbirth, reflecting on past experiences.
